question: A cheap dominant (HGRAVS01 low-rank) plus sparse exceptions, executed as ONE fused operator rather than two passes — does the fusion traffic save move a Qwen3.8 decode token on this M3 Ultra?
answer: NOT_WORTH_BUILDING. Fusion guaranteed save is 1,310,720 B = 2199.6 ns at 595.9 GB/s (0.0072% of 30.606 ms). The approximation family is already refuted as a byte/quality lever except as a Q80 down_proj COMPONENT; the novel fusion claim is dead on accounting. Do not write the shader.

hits.headline: The best correction topology is the one that carries NO index at all. A single function-fitted binary PLANE at 1.25 b/elem beats every index-carrying topology at 1.0 b/elem on every site (57.8% mean reduction against COLUMN's 30.9% and SCATTERED's 30.4% across all budgets), and unlike them it already has a kernel measured UNDER the decode budget (binary_planes_k2, 0.6647 ps/element, -17.9%).

operator.name: fused_hgravs01_csr_matvec
operator.scope: mlp.down_proj × 64 on Qwen3.8; other organs out of scope
operator.math: W ∈ R^{5120×17408}, x ∈ R^{17408} (post-SwiGLU). R ∈ R^{160×17408}, L ∈ R^{5120×160} packed HGRAVS01 3-bit g64. S stored CSR: row_ptr, col_idx, 1-bit residual signs, f16 scale. y = L (R x) + S_csr x, with S_csr the residual after the low-rank fit, not a second copy of W.

access.R_codes_scales: row-major grouped; 8-wide LSB unpack; coalesced sequential
access.L_codes_scales: row-major; 160 cols, 8-wide; coalesced (the simd3 8-unpack exists specifically because L is 160-col)
access.x_in_R: length 17408, sequential, 69632 B — cache-resident vs SLC
access.x_in_CSR: gather x[col] from the same 69632 B vector. Not a 50 MiB weight gather. G070/NS-032 10-of-512 expert gather (150.2 GB/s) is a different pattern (large tensors). Here the working set is 70 KiB.
access.CSR_indices_signs: streamed in row order — coalesced. Index share of expanded CSR is ~97% (u32 index vs 1-bit sign).

access.lane0_serial_csr: at 2% density, 348.2 nnz/row serial on lane 0 while 255 threads idle. That occupancy tax is the sparse half's real cost on this hardware, not DRAM coalescing of x.

Either r160 is already enough (sparse is waste) or it is not (sparse 2% cannot close). Both kill the fused family.

kill_rules: GPU(B) >= GPU(A): LR occupancy eats the byte win on this launch geometry (20 TGs on 60 cores for R).
GPU(CSR @ 2%) < 0.01 * GPU(A): fusing CSR cannot move the token; fusion-specific value is dead.
GPU(C) >= GPU(A): adding sparse makes two-pass slower than incumbent even before quality.
arm E fails q3 held-out: do not write the fused shader.

predicted_from_accounting.prediction: Fusion save is 64 * 20_480 B y-reread = 1,310,720 B = 2199.6 ns at 595.9 GB/s = 0.0072% of the 30.606 ms token. CSR @ 2% itself is hundreds of µs of *weight* traffic that fusion does not remove.

s011.rule: S011 §4 (lane contract): a design that does not reduce at least one of bytes, operations, dispatches, materialization, synchronization or traffic is INCOMPLETE.

synchronization.vs_incumbent: SAME 1 CB; extra device mid[640 B] between two dispatches

s011.caveat: Bytes and operations REDUCE only if down_proj is replaced. That replacement is a quality bet this family has already lost on gate/up and at matched bits. The *novel* axis (fusion vs two-pass) reduces dispatches by 64 and traffic by 1,310,720 B guaranteed. Complete on paper, not worth the kernel.

what_it_would_win: If r160 on Qwen3.8 down were q3-healthy, replacing 64 Q4 down GEMVs cuts 3,030,384,640 B → 97,976,320 B of down weights (0.1374 BPW complete, not the 0.13 slogan) and cuts down MACs to 0.040×. Bandwidth scaling of the whole token would be ~24.19 ms (41.3 tok/s), which would beat MLX 35.51 — *if* quality and R-stage occupancy hold. That win is LR-on-down, already named in QWEN38_BPW_DESCENT, not fusion.
Fusion vs two-pass saves 64 dispatches and 1,310,720 B of y re-read (2199.6 ns at the 595.9 GB/s roof, 0.0072% of the token).
what_it_risks: Quality: G034 rank-803 at *matched q3 bits* is 2.93× q3 error. r160 is 0.137 BPW, 5× below q3 and 3.1% of 5120 rows. G1-SHARE captured 41.9% energy at r512 on gate. Qwen3.8 BPW descent never scored HGRAVS01 hold-cosine on 5120×17408.

Q80 inversion does not transfer: QWEN38_BPW_DESCENT measured Q80 expert 512×2048 at rank 160 as 31% of rows; Qwen3.8 down 5120×17408 at rank 160 is 3.1% of rows on a 34× wider K. Frontier W is [2048,512] — r160/512 = 31%, r160/5120 = 3.1%.
Phase B hybrid: q3+LR correction generalizes but ADDS bytes (107% of q3). q2+LR cannot catch q3 inside a reasonable budget. Sparse 2% on a rank-160 hole is that experiment with a worse dominant.
MLP distillation, the named surviving avenue after Phase B, is NO-GO at +0.4206 held-out / 72% bytes.
R-stage occupancy: 20 TGs on 60 cores (0.33 TG/core). NS-019: remaining cost of factored down is occupancy, not reconstruct-W.
CSR lane-0 serial at ~348 nnz/row is occupancy poison the Q80 2% recipe does not pay (there nnz/row ~4 on 512-col experts).

G070: SCATTERED spends 60% of budget on coordinates; a function-fitted binary PLANE at 1.25 b/elem beat every index-carrying topology. CSR-of-exceptions is the topology G070 already killed on kernel cost when it used atomics; lane-0 serial is the other way to lose occupancy.
NS-006: fewer stored bytes is not a faster token if reconstruction/occupancy eats the win. G043 already classified compact q3 as NET-LOSS on this vehicle.

Writing the fused shader would add a representation the sealed NR cannot account (n16clos: LowRank + SparseResidual = schema-change). Injection of uncounted structure leaves complete_bpw stuck at 4.253.
expected_value.cheapest_kill: Arm E of the microbenchmark: one-layer SVD / r160 functional rel-fro on real post-SwiGLU X versus q3, plus isolated q80_sparse_q1_apply_csr_simd at 348 nnz/row on 5120 outputs. Do not write Metal until both numbers exist. Predicted fusion save 2199.6 ns already kills the fusion-specific claim; arm E kills the representation claim.
